title: Francis at the shut gate
hookLine: Francis says perfect joy is being turned away cold and wet and staying patient (Little Flowers 8)
carry: perfect joy has nothing to prove

cards: Winter. Two friars walk a long road in bitter cold, Brother Leo out in front and Francis behind. Francis calls ahead.
Brother Leo, write this down. If our brothers everywhere set a great example of holiness, that is not perfect joy. He calls again.
If a brother healed the sick and gave sight to the blind, write it down: that is not perfect joy. If he knew every language and all the scriptures, and could tell the future, not perfect joy.
If he preached so well that unbelievers turned to God, not perfect joy. At last Leo, amazed, asks: Father, then what is perfect joy?

teach.b: Francis answers with a scene. We arrive at our own friary at night, soaked with rain, stiff with cold, spattered with mud and hungry, and we knock at the gate. The brother on the door says, Who are you?
We say, two of your brothers. And he says, You're lying. You're a pair of tramps who go around fooling people and taking the alms of the poor.
Go away. And he leaves us outside in the snow and the rain.
If we bear that patiently, without grumbling, and think that perhaps this porter knows us as we truly are, write it down, Brother Leo: that is perfect joy.
The story pushes further: they knock again and are driven off; again, and are beaten. Still, perfect joy. Why?

teach.h: NOTHING OF OUR OWN TO BOAST OF.
teach.b: Everything on his first list is God's gift, so nobody can boast of it. He quotes Paul: "what hast thou that thou didst not receive?"
The one thing a person can bring of their own is to bear a hard thing patiently, for love of Christ. And Paul again: "God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ."
This isn't a call to stay in harm's way. It's a story about pride. The usual move is to rehearse the speech: do you know who I am?
Francis's joy is not needing to win that argument. Yesterday he was free of things.
Today he's free of his own reputation.

how: Franciscans and other Christians tell the story of perfect joy from the Little Flowers of St Francis as a lesson in humility and patience; the story itself ends with Paul's words about glorying only in the cross.

o: the happiness of heaven after a holy death
bearing a rejection patiently, with nothing to prove
a feeling of bliss from working great miracles

p: calls them tramps and shuts the gate
what hast thou that thou didst not receive

s: for Francis, working miracles is perfect joy
it's on his list of what isn't: those are God's gifts, so no one can boast of them.
in the story, the porter doesn't believe them and shuts them out
he calls them liars and leaves them in the snow and rain.
perfect joy means everything going right
it's bearing the cold gate patiently, for love, with nothing to prove.

games.q: you're Francis, soaked and frozen at your own friary gate. the porter calls you a liar and shuts you out. what does Francis call perfect joy?
o: pound on the gate until he lets you in.
go and tell the other brothers what he did.
games.why: bearing it patiently, even thinking the porter may know you truly: write it down, Brother Leo, that is perfect joy.

practice: Recall a recent time you were brushed off, a message ignored, a flat no, someone who didn't believe you, and notice the old speech start up: the defense, the comeback. Don't deliver it; let it run out, like rain off a roof.

If you pray, hold that moment before God; if you don't, just breathe, and let the door stay shut. And if someone is truly hurting you, this isn't a door to wait at: please reach someone you trust, or local emergency help.

wordCard.voice: Perfect joy. Francis's name for bearing a hard rejection patiently, for love, with nothing to prove.

orig.note: Italian, not Latin: perfect joy, as the Little Flowers (Fioretti) names it.

carryVoice: Your line: perfect joy has nothing to prove. Every gift was received; the patience is ours to give. Rest well, and see you tomorrow.
